title: Count the piggy bank: guess first, then count
description: Before you open a piggy bank or savings jar, guess what is inside — in writing. Then count it properly, in sorted stacks. The gap between the guess and the truth is the lesson.

body.heading: Guess, then open
paragraphs: Pick up the bank, feel its weight, shake it gently, and write down your best guess of the total — and how confident you feel, from 'wild guess' to 'almost sure'. Most people are surprised in one direction or the other, because coins are deceptively heavy and notes weigh nothing.

Empty everything onto a table. Sort coins by denomination into stacks of ten, count the stacks, then add notes. Sorting first makes the count checkable: if the total looks wrong, you can recount one stack instead of starting again.

body.heading: What to do with the truth
paragraphs: Compare the counted total with the guess and note the difference. Then decide the money's job before it evaporates: a named goal, a bank deposit, or a split between saving and spending.
Write the new starting total and today's date on a slip inside the refilled bank. Next count, you will know exactly how much the habit added — and your guess will be sharper, too.

takeaway: Guess the piggy bank's total in writing, then sort, stack and count it — the surprise gap teaches more about your money than the total does.
materials: A piggy bank or savings jar with contents
Paper and pen for the guess and the tally
supervision: A parent or partner double-checks the count with younger savers and helps decide where the counted money goes next.
safetyNotes: Wash hands after handling lots of coins, and keep small coins away from toddlers, who may swallow them.
Count at home in private, and put the money away promptly rather than leaving it out on display.
